title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the GF IX / IX bis notes of July 1986, an 'atelier' is a set A with three pieces of structure: an incidence or face-type order (⊲ strict, ⊴ large), a relation X ˚≪ Y (a 'strict/interior' smallness relation), and a dimension-like function |·|. From these a derived relation ≪ is built. From this page it looks like X ≪ Y iff there exists Y' with X ˚≪ Y' ⊴ Y. The page opens 'GF IX bis', a complement to earlier pages (p. 46 and p. 27), and states the programme: find one notion of morphism of ateliers covering three types of situation. Only the first situation is treated here: sub-ateliers.

Definition (Sousat). A subset A' ⊂ A is a sub-atelier if, whenever X ˚≪ Y' ⊲ Y with X, Y ∈ A', then also Y' ∈ A'. This is a convexity or saturation condition: an intermediate face that witnesses ≪ between two members of A' must itself lie in A'.

Claim. With the induced ⊴, ˚≪ and |·|, A' is again an atelier. Moreover the intrinsically defined ≪_{A'} equals the restriction of ≪_A. Grothendieck notes that this compatibility is essentially equivalent to Sousat: the factorisation witnessing X ≪_A Y must be realisable inside A'.

Example 1. Let 𝔓 be a 'préfigure': a subset whose ⊲-closure 𝔓̄ is a 'figure', i.e. its elements are pairwise in the relation ≍. Then the open shadow Omb°(𝔓) = {X ∈ A | X ˚≪ 𝔓} is a sub-atelier; the proof is referred back to GF IX p. 27.

Example 1 bis. A préfigure 𝔓 is itself a sub-atelier, and with the induced structure it is a 'quiddité', apparently the degenerate or discrete kind of atelier. Proof: if X ˚≪ Y' ⊲ Y with X, Y ∈ 𝔓 ⊂ 𝔓̄, then Y' ∈ 𝔓̄ because 𝔓̄ is ⊲-closed. Inside the figure 𝔓̄ the relation forces X = Y', hence Y' ∈ 𝔓.

Next page. It continues with 'residual ateliers' (strict and broad sense) as further sub-ateliers, and asks whether the induced map Σ_{A'} → Σ_A is an embedding.

Purpose. This is foundational bookkeeping for a home-made combinatorial-geometric axiomatics of 'ateliers'. It is apparently tied to Grothendieck's 1986 'GF' (géométrie floue?) manuscripts, which aim at a combinatorial or tame description of figures, shadows and residues. Here he prepares the definition of morphisms of ateliers.
errors: No outright error is visible. The argument in Ex 1 bis relies on an unstated property of figures: that X ˚≪ Y' with X, Y' in a figure forces X = Y'. Its validity depends on the definition of ≍ given in GF IX, which is not visible here.
The parenthetical claim that Sousat is equivalent to ≪_{A'} being induced by ≪_A presupposes that ≪ is defined as the composite ˚≪ ∘ ⊴. That definition is not restated on this page.

ideas.what: Sub-atelier defined by a saturation/convexity condition on factorisations X ˚≪ Y' ⊲ Y
ideas.modern_name: Convex or interval-closed subposet; full sub-structure closed under witnesses of a composite relation (cf. order-convex subsets, convex subcomplexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: General order theory folklore; the specific 'atelier' axiomatics is Grothendieck's own and unpublished

ideas.what: Open shadow Omb°(𝔓) of a préfigure is a sub-atelier
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of a star or open neighbourhood of a simplex/face in a cell complex being a subcomplex-like object

ideas.what: A préfigure is itself a sub-atelier and is a 'quiddité' (degenerate atelier)
Programme: a notion of morphism of ateliers unifying sub-ateliers, residual ateliers and further situations
ideas.modern_name: Choosing morphisms for a category of incidence-type structures (cf. morphisms of posets / cell complexes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to define morphisms of ateliers that handle three types of situation (sub-ateliers being the first). The notes here only start the first case, and the whole 'atelier' axiomatics appears absent from the literature.
missed.quote: Je suis intéressé par trois types de situations, que je voudrais pouvoir exprimer par une notion de morphismes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mainly historical interest. It documents a 1986 attempt at a combinatorial foundation of 'figures', 'shadows' and 'residues'. It could be compared with later combinatorial approaches to stratified or tame spaces (face posets, exit-path posets). The mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The framework (ateliers, figures, préfigures, ombres, quiddités) is unknown in the literature, which is mildly notable historically. The content of the page itself, however, is routine verification of closure properties of subsets.
transcription_corrections: The margin note reads approximately 'Compl. au GF [XII?] p. 46 et ... p. 27'; the roman numeral near the top is struck through or partly overwritten and is uncertain.

Ex 1 bis proof should read roughly: '(En effet, si X ˚≪ Y' ⊲ Y, avec X, Y ∈ 𝔓 ⊂ 𝔓̄, comme Y' ∈ 𝔓̄, on a X = Y', donc Y' ∈ 𝔓.)'. The machine version garbles the inclusion 𝔓 ⊂ 𝔓̄ and the membership Y' ∈ 𝔓̄.
'(ce qui est équivalent [?] précisément par Sousat)' likely reads '(ce qui est assuré précisément par Sousat)' or similar.
In Ex 1 the condition is 'X, Y ∈ 𝔓 ⇒ X ≍ Y'; the symbol is ≍ (or a similar 'compatible' sign) as written.
